title: Total blood volume per kg body mass, adult humans and horses
source: Oberholzer L et al., Determinants and reference values for blood volume and total haemoglobin mass in women and men, Am J Hematol 2024;99:88-98 (abstract, carbon monoxide rebreathing); Wikipedia Blood volume for the textbook 70 and 65 mL/kg; a Brazilian Thoroughbred study (Pesquisa Agropecuaria Brasileira abstract on the Embrapa site, 51Cr red cells) and Hinchcliff 1991 as quoted on a PharmPK list for horses. Nadler 1962 has no abstract on PubMed, so its figures did not open.
rows: 319 men aged 10 to 93 y, BMI 14 to 41, carbon monoxide rebreathing; mean +/- SD 10.8
Low and High are mean -/+ SD. The sample includes ages from 10 y. The authors say the values may hold only for CO rebreathing; per kg of lean mass men were 105.3 +/- 11.2.
263 women, same study and method; mean +/- SD 11.3
Low and High are mean -/+ SD. Per kg of lean mass women were 110.9 +/- 12.5.
Wikipedia body text; cites clinicaltrials.gov NCT02972294 and a University of Iowa page, not a radiolabel paper
The page's own table lists 75 for men, so the page disagrees with itself. Nadler 1962 (radiolabel) was not opened.

Blood volume, healthy adult Thoroughbred horse
11 healthy Thoroughbreds (plus 5 with equine infectious anaemia at 107.71), 51Cr-tagged red cells
Radioisotope red-cell method. Horses have a splenic red-cell store, so the figure depends on the horse's state and the method.

Second-hand, from a forum post quoting the paper; the paper was not opened. Low and High are mean -/+ 5.1.
